source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Heparin is continued mainly to prevent warfarin from raising the INR too quickly, and it can be stopped as soon as the first warfarin dose is absorbed.","B":"Warfarin provides immediate full anticoagulation, while heparin is added temporarily to reduce the risk of bleeding during the first several treatment days of therapy.","C":"The overlap is used because warfarin prevents heparin from affecting laboratory tests, allowing both drugs to be stopped once the INR first begins to rise.","D":"Warfarin requires several days for full anticoagulant effect, so full-dose heparin is overlapped for about 4–5 days and until the desired INR response is reached."}}
source_row.rationale: Warfarin labeling states that its full anticoagulant effect takes several days and recommends overlapping full-dose heparin and warfarin for about 4–5 days and until the desired INR response is achieved. Option D matches that rationale. Option A misstates the purpose of heparin. Option B incorrectly says warfarin is immediately fully effective. Option C incorrectly describes laboratory interference and an inadequate stopping criterion.
